11. Tooke the ſtoner.) Iacob trauailing into a ſtrange countrie went in ſuch
pocre eſtate, the better to hide his departure trom Eſau, who otherwiſe might
haue killed him by the way. It was alfo thus diſpoſed by God, that Iacobe
faith and confidence might, to his greater merit, be exerciſed : aud that Gods
prouidence might more manifeſtly appeare, as it did in his returne after twentie
yeares, when with moſt gratetul mind he recounted Gods beneſits ſaying (Gen.
32:) With my ſtafte I paſſed ouer thit Iordan, aud now with two troups I doc
returne.
12.ladder. † He that was in temporal diſtreſſe was maruelonſly comforted
ſpiritually, by ſeeing ladder that reached from the carth to heauen : An-
gels paſſing vp and downe the ſame, and the Sonne of God leaning vpon it,
as he that reigneth both in heauen and earth, who in particular promifed him
and his ſred that whole land, that he and his fred ſhould be bleſfed, vea that
in Hir Seed Al nations ſhould be bleſſed, and that he wuuld keep and protect
him where ſoeuer he went. How al this was performed is briefty reherſed in
the booke of wiſdorne chap. 10.
18. Erected it, powring oyie. † To erect a ſtone, and powre oyle vpon it, was
no wiſe ſuperſtitious in Iacob. Neither did he learne it of Idolaters: for he
abhorred and deteſted al idololatrical abſeruances. But as S. Iuſtinus Martyr S.
Clement of Alexandria, Origen, Euſebiue, and others teſtifie, idololatrical
ſuperſtition did rather imitate true religious ceremonics. For the diuel alwayer
affecting that honour which he ſeeth done to God, perſwaded thoſe whom
he ſeduced and hlinded with errours, to ſtrue him in fuch manner of
external rites, as God was ſerued, that therby he might either haue like
